gloss: business failure; corporate collapse; management breakdown

definitions.explanation: The failure or collapse of a business, typically due to financial difficulties. A formal term frequently used in news and business contexts.

examples.japanese: ⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{経営|けいえい}{破綻|はたん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{追|お}い{込|こ}まれた→追い込む：06371_oikomu⟧。
examples.english: The company was driven into business failure.

examples.japanese: {経営|けいえい}{破綻|はたん}⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{銀行|ぎんこう}→銀行：00578_ginkou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{預金者|よきんしゃ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{不安|ふあん}→不安：00836_fuan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じている→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧。
examples.english: Depositors of the failed bank are feeling anxious.

examples.japanese: {過大|かだい}な⟦{投資|とうし}→投資：04711_toushi⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{売上|うりあげ}→売上：04102_uriage⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{減少|げんしょう}→減少：02719_genshou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{重|かさ}なり→重なる：02038_kasanaru⟧、{経営|けいえい}{破綻|はたん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{至|いた}った→至る：02009_itaru⟧。
examples.english: Excessive investment combined with declining sales led to corporate collapse.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{経営|けいえい}→経営：02740_keiei⟧ (management; business operation) + ⟦{破綻|はたん}→破綻：09066_hatan⟧ (failure; collapse; breakdown). A formal term seen frequently in news reports, financial articles, and legal contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {経営|けいえい}{破綻|はたん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{陥|おちい}る→陥る：14537_ochiiru⟧: to fall into business failure
- {経営|けいえい}{破綻|はたん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{追|お}い{込|こ}まれる→追い込む：06371_oikomu⟧: to be driven to collapse
- {経営|けいえい}{破綻|はたん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{至|いた}る→至る：02009_itaru⟧: to result in business failure
- {経営|けいえい}{破綻|はたん}⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{企業|きぎょう}→企業：00225_kigyou⟧: a company that has failed
- {経営|けいえい}{破綻|はたん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{防|ふせ}ぐ→防ぐ：02409_fusegu⟧: to prevent business failure

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{倒産|とうさん}→倒産：03452_tousan⟧: bankruptcy; going out of business — more common in everyday speech, specifically means ceasing operations
- ⟦{破産|はさん}→破産：03555_hasan⟧: bankruptcy (legal) — a legal declaration of inability to pay debts
- ⟦{廃業|はいぎょう}→廃業：20645_haigyou⟧: closing a business — voluntary cessation, not necessarily due to financial failure
